_schema: One entry per exercise, oldest first. Read/write this file whenever you generate or grade an exercise in this repo -- pull latest before reading, push after writing, so the daily generator and any grading session stay in sync.

_fields.date: MM-DD-YYYY, matches the exercise folder's date prefix
_fields.category: one of: code-review | debugging | architecture-tradeoffs | typescript-modeling | react-state-performance
_fields.domain_or_topic: short tag for what the exercise was actually about, e.g. 'pub-sub / effect cleanup', 'discriminated unions', 'memoization' -- used to keep a revisit close to the original rather than just same-category-different-thing
_fields.outcome: pending | struggled | solid | mastered -- 'pending' until Joel submits a solution and gets graded
_fields.notes: 1-2 sentences on what specifically went wrong or well, written at grading time
_fields.revisit: true if this concept should be brought back in a near-future exercise before it's considered done; false once revisited-and-solid or never needed

_generation_rules: If the most recent graded entry has outcome 'struggled': do NOT advance difficulty or rotate to a new category. Generate an exercise in the SAME category, touching the SAME or a closely adjacent domain_or_topic, at the same or one point lower difficulty -- a variation, not a repeat, that re-exercises the same underlying concept.

If any entry has revisit=true and hasn't been revisited yet (no later entry references the same domain_or_topic as a deliberate follow-up), prioritize bringing that concept back within the next 2-3 exercises, even if it means holding off on category rotation for a day.

If the most recent graded entry has outcome 'solid' or 'mastered': advance normally -- rotate to a category not used in the last 1-2 days, increase difficulty by 0-1 point (cap ~7-8/10, then hold/vary).
If the most recent entry is still 'pending' (Joel hasn't been graded on it yet), do not lower difficulty; proceed with normal rotation at the same difficulty as that pending entry.

When generating a revisit exercise, say so honestly in that day's entry's domain_or_topic (e.g. 'effect cleanup -- revisit of 09-21') but do NOT spoil this in the README the way the original exercise didn't spoil its own flaw.
